images.caption: Figure 2:Performance of the self-modulating update rules relative to their paired gated baselines. (a) Win rate by sequence length, aggregated across datasets and model families. (b) Win rate by dataset, aggregated across sequence lengths and model families. (c) Median relative MSE improvement [Eq.˜3] by model family, aggregated across datasets and sequence lengths. Dashed lines in (a) and (b) mark a 50% win rate; the horizontal line in (c) marks zero improvement.

Figure 3:Final test MSE of each self-modulating rule versus its paired gated baseline across all datasets, sequence lengths, and model families: (a) Only-new, (b) Only-old, (c) Full, and (d) CMG. The diagonal indicates equal MSE; points below it favor self-modulation. Colors denote model families, and markers denote sequence lengths.
Figure 4:Test MSE versus training epoch for QKANFWP atN=64N=64: (a) Jaynes–Cummings and (b) transmon–resonator. Curves show the mean over five seeds, and shaded bands show±1\pm 1standard deviation.

Figure 5:Mean test MSE for direct multi-step forecasting with QKANFWP and QKAN-QKANFWP atN=64N=64, separated by dataset, forecast horizon, and update rule. Values are averaged over five seeds; colors encode MSE on a logarithmic scale. CMG uses one low-rank-generated gate matrix, whereas Full uses separate old- and new-modulation matrices.

Figure 6:Relative MSE improvement over the paired gated baseline [Eq.˜3] for direct multi-step forecasting atN=64N=64. Rows group update rules within QKANFWP and QKAN-QKANFWP; columns group forecast horizons within the Jaynes–Cummings and transmon–resonator datasets. Values are computed from mean MSE over five seeds. Red denotes improvement, whereas blue denotes degradation.

Figure 7:Direct multi-step forecasts on the transmon–resonator test set for QKAN-QKANFWP withN=64N=64andH=8H=8. Columns compare scalar-gated, Full, and CMG updates; rows show model checkpoints after 50 and 100 epochs. Curves show the mean prediction over five seeds with±1\pm 1standard-deviation bands and the ground truth. Shading identifies the first input window and first eight-step output block.
